sides.name: Roman Republic and Numidia (Scipio, Masinissa)
sides.note: Tech override per derived:tech-anchor (SOURCES.md anchor table, interpolated by year); air and cyber 0 = derived:absent-in-era. Ratings per derived:rating-rubric. c. 29,000-30,000: 23,000-24,000 infantry (incl. Masinissa's 6,000 Numidian foot) and 6,100 cavalry (1,500 Italian, 4,600 Numidian). Line/velites split derived from the manipular ratio. Scipio's flexible manipular legion mapped to roman-imperial. Command 0.9: Scipio. Training 0.8: veterans of Spain and the Cannae legions. riverCrossing false: the armies met on open ground, no river (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Battle_of_Zama).

sides.name: Carthage (Hannibal)
sides.note: Tech override per derived:tech-anchor (SOURCES.md anchor table, interpolated by year); air and cyber 0 = derived:absent-in-era. Ratings per derived:rating-rubric. c. 40,000 or 50,000: 36,000-46,000 infantry in three lines (mercenaries, Carthaginian/Libyan levy, 15,000-20,000 veterans of Italy), 4,000 cavalry (half Numidian), 80+ elephants. Split derived. Mapped to archetype-classical-infantry: weak cavalry, infantry-line battle. Training 0.5: mix of veterans and raw levies. Morale 0.6: new levies wavered. prepared false: both armies deployed in three lines in the open for a pitched battle, Hannibal opening with his elephants (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Battle_of_Zama).

outcome.note: Roman victory. Polybius: Carthaginians 20,000 killed + 20,000 captured; Romans at least 1,500 killed and many wounded. Roman mid 4,000 assumes ~1.5 wounded per killed (derived). Ancient figures, grade C. Exact site of the battle is disputed; coordinates are the commonly cited one.
